hook_text: Fill made everyone thin. Fit made them the right shape. The difference is one number.
clip_script:
A family has a favourite photograph, 10 centimetres by 15, and wants it big for the lounge wall. The print shop offers an enlargement with the short side at 50 centimetres. A Grade 8 in the family checks the long side: scale factor 50 over 10, which is 5; long side 15 times 5, which is 75 centimetres. Every length five times, every angle unchanged, every face the right shape. Similar.

Her cousin has the same photograph as a phone wallpaper and complains that everyone looks too thin. The phone has stretched the picture 2,4 times one way and 1,6 times the other. Two different factors: angles change, a square frame becomes a rectangle, faces go wrong. Not similar. One scale factor in every direction is what similar means.
visual_style: A small photograph growing evenly into a wall print beside the same photograph squashed onto a phone screen, with a square frame in the picture turning into a tall rectangle
pacing: two parallel beats, then the contrast
call_to_action: Open the full session to test shapes for congruence and similarity and calculate with scale factors.
